name: Turumba Messaging
tagline: From content to connection to community.

company.name: Agelgel Technologies
company.note: Brand Bible spells this 'Agelgel Technonlogies'. Confirm legal spelling.

overview.summary: Turumba is a multi-channel messaging platform built to help content creators, churches, and ministry organizations take their message where people already are.
overview.origin: Invented by local believers in Ethiopia in collaboration with Christian missionaries across Africa and Asia, built out of their own ministry needs and with great personal sacrifice.
overview.whatItDoes: Aggregates WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, email and more into one dashboard, and distributes follow-up to the whole body of Christ, not just paid staff.
overview.problem: Discipleship does not happen when someone visits a website. It happens through relationships and conversation on the platforms people already use.
overview.before: A creator with large reach, no capacity for personal follow-up, and an audience that never becomes a community.
overview.after: Content moves to connection, and connection moves to community.
overview.heritage: Turumba 1.0 trained over 60,000 digital missionaries and processed up to 150,000 messages per minute at peak. Turumba 2.0 rebuilds seven years of learning on a modern architecture.
overview.coreConviction: The message is the product, not the technology.
overview.mission: Uberize connections and community with your content. Empower content creators, churches, and ministry organizations to take their message where people already are, through the messaging platforms they use every day.
overview.vision: A world where every believer, from an individual content creator to a denomination of ten thousand churches, has the tools to do sustainable, relational digital ministry at scale. Where if you have a cell phone, you can be a missionary. Where the body of Christ is empowered to move from content to connection to community, reaching the last, the least, and the lost through the platforms where their people live.

primary.name: Content creators and student groups
primary.description: Individual pastors, campus ministry leaders, and digital missionaries creating content on social media, under an organization or denomination. They generate reach but lack capacity for personal follow-up at scale.

primary.name: Small ministry organizations
primary.description: Field teams closest to the ground who need affordable, purpose-built digital outreach tools they could never build on their own.

primary.name: Large ministry organizations
primary.description: Need enterprise-grade multi-channel messaging, on-premise deployment for security, and a replacement for aging tools like Echo Global at a fraction of the cost.

primary.name: Denominational church leaders
primary.description: Leaders of denominations and church networks who want to equip every church with digital outreach tools at negligible per-church cost.

primary.name: Secular content creators and businesses
primary.description: Individuals and businesses needing professional multi-channel chat management and automation, served at full commercial rates. This revenue subsidizes ministry access.

audience.notFor: Teams whose goal is only to make a sale.

differentials: Built from the ground up for ministry
On-premise and self-hosted deployment for closed-country security
Seamless switching of social media accounts after government censorship without losing contacts or ministry strategy
Pricing that does not penalize scale, from a team of 5 to a denomination of 13,000 churches
Follow-up distributed across the whole body of Christ

competitors.name: Echo Global
competitors.strengths: Established in ministry space, proven at scale
competitors.weaknesses: Aging architecture, expensive at scale, no on-premise option, degrading

competitors.name: ManyChat
competitors.weaknesses: Too expensive for ministry budgets, data must be deleted to manage costs, drives sales rather than discipleship

competitors.name: Chatwoot
competitors.weaknesses: Not ministry-focused, no journey builder, limited multi-tenant support

competitors.name: Zendesk / Intercom
competitors.weaknesses: Wrong pricing model for ministry, no understanding of field realities

personality.archetype: The Co-laborer / The Herald (proposal, not in source)

negative.name: Echo Global

negative.name: Staged stock imagery

promise.toMinistryPartners: We will never penalize the scale of your ministry. Turumba is built so that growth makes things easier and more affordable, not harder and more expensive. Your content, your contacts, and your conversation history belong to you. We will always go where people are, and we will always design for the last, least, and lost.
promise.toContentCreators: We believe in you and the content God gave you. We exist to help you move from content to connection to community, empowering you to engage your audience and entrust the body of Christ to disciple them. You create. We bridge.
promise.toAllCustomers: A message deserves a great messenger. We promise to keep the message, not the technology, at the center of everything we build.
promise.synthesizingPhrase: Turumba exists so that every message finds its people.

cannotBe: Anything that penalizes scale or makes growth harder
guardrails.litmusTest: If it talks about us more than about the creator, ministry leader, or church, it is wrong.

identity.statement: We are for the content creator, the pastor, the campus ministry leader, the digital missionary. We are not a software company. The content God gave you matters more than any platform. We exist because a message deserves a great messenger.
identity.essence: We built the bridge between your content and your community.

tonalRules: Talk about the creator, the ministry leader, and the church more than about ourselves.
Be confident and visionary: 'We believe in what you do.'
Stay grounded and practical. Pair big claims with a concrete mechanism.
Use spiritual depth without religious jargon.
Speak like a passionate co-laborer, not a software vendor.
Use 'we' for Turumba and 'you' for the creator, ministry leader, or church.
Lead with the mission, not the feature list.
With secular audiences, shift to a professional and modern register that leads with capability and value.
Say plainly that we do not exist to sell software.

accent.usage: Highlights key information and guides attention. Large text only on light grounds.

colors.accentNote: Accent ramps in the Brand Bible repeat the blue ramp hex values. Regenerate true ramps before shipping.
colors.logoColors: Full color on white in approved blue, deep blue, and violet. White on colored or black backgrounds.

primary.use: Headings, body copy, interface elements, supporting content

secondary.use: Editorial layouts, supporting content, greater typographic contrast. Always complements DM Sans.

rules: Use display styles sparingly, for major sections only.
Avoid unnecessary variation between text styles.

logo.logomark: Circular mark containing a stylized trumpet line. Used alone when space is limited or the brand is well established.
logo.logotype: 'Turumba' with 'Messaging' and a TM mark. Used for first impressions, formal communications, and wherever recognition is essential.
logo.clearspace: Minimum equal to the height of the symbol on every side.
logo.coBranding: Both brands sit together clearly and equally. The 'T' of the logotype defines clear space and distance to the partner mark.
misuse: Add strokes, outlines, emboss, 3D effects, or drop shadows
Change the colors of individual characters
Modify any part, or scale or move parts independently
Place on busy imagery without a solid container

principles.name: Recognizable
principles.description: Distinctive, authentic, and easy to remember.

principles.name: People-first
principles.description: People, relationships, and human experiences at the center.

principles.name: Forward-looking
principles.description: Modern, optimistic imagery that communicates progress, possibility, and growth.

subjects: People and users in real moments
The Turumba trumpet as a heritage object
photographyAndIllustration.lighting: Soft natural daylight, often from windows, with balanced exposure and a clean, warm look.
do: Keep the subject simple and in focus.
Keep color true to life, or reduce color.
Use images with a solid background and put text in the space beside the subject.
dont: Use busy images where subject and background colors blend.
Manipulate hue, saturation, brightness, or contrast unrealistically.
Overlay text on the subject. If unavoidable, use an overlay.

artDirection.directionStatement: The identity should communicate a bridge between a creator and their people. Every decision should put the message ahead of the technology.
artDirection.visualTerritory: The sound of the Turumba trumpet. Deep blue fields that shift into light. A single human subject in natural light. Vertical pulses of sound running across the surface.

pattern.concept: Inspired by the sound of the Turumba trumpet. Each vertical line is a pulse of sound, a message sent out and heard. Varied heights and spacing show communication traveling across the platform.

artDirection.layout: Section dividers use a large numeral, a thin horizontal rule, an arrow, and a large white title on the blue gradient and pattern. Content pages use white or #F7F7F7 grounds, blue headings, and gray body text.

willNotUse: Names that imply the software replaces the messenger
Names that frame the product as sales automation
